steps: Season the chicken breast with salt, pepper and a pinch of oregano, then grill or pan-fry over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes per side until cooked through.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, then slice.
Roughly chop the cucumber and tomatoes into chunks and thinly slice the red onion.
Toss the cucumber, tomato, onion and kalamata olives together in a bowl.
Crumble the feta over the top, add the sliced chicken, and drizzle with the olive oil and a scatter of oregano.
Whisk the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a nonstick frying pan over medium heat and soften the diced pepper for 2-3 minutes.
Add the ham and warm through for 1 minute.
Pour in the whisked eggs, tilting the pan to spread evenly, and cook for 2-3 minutes until the base sets.
Fold the omelette in half once the top is just set and slide onto a plate.
Serve alongside the leaves, tomato and cucumber salad.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C).
Toss the sweet potato cubes in a little oil and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until tender and caramelised at the edges.
Season the chicken thighs and roast on a separate tray for 30-35 minutes until the skin is golden and the juices run clear.
Wilt the spinach in a hot pan for 1-2 minutes, then squeeze out any excess liquid.
Divide the chicken, sweet potato and spinach between 4 containers.
Drizzle each portion with tahini and a squeeze of lemon juice before serving.
Toss the chicken thighs with shawarma spices (cumin, paprika, turmeric, cinnamon, garlic) and a little oil; marinate for 10 minutes if time allows.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken for 6-8 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Cook the basmati rice according to the packet instructions and fluff with a fork.
Whisk the tahini with a little water and lemon juice until smooth and pourable.
Chop the tomato, cucumber and onion into a chopped salad.
Divide the rice, chicken, chopped salad and pickles between 4 bowls and drizzle with the tahini sauce.
Spoon the hummus onto one side of a plate.
Warm the falafel briefly if needed and arrange the 4 pieces alongside the hummus.
Add a mound of tabbouleh, a handful of olives and sliced cucumber.
Warm the pita for 30 seconds on each side in a dry pan and serve alongside the mezze.
Thread the chicken pieces onto skewers and season with oregano, lemon zest, garlic and olive oil; marinate briefly if time allows.
Grill or pan-fry the skewers over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred and cooked through.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions, then stir through lemon zest and juice.
Stir the yogurt, grated cucumber (squeezed dry) and crushed garlic together for the tzatziki, and season to taste.
Divide the lemon rice, souvlaki and Greek salad between 4 plates and serve with the tzatziki.
Preheat the oven to 185°C/Gas mark 5.
Peel the onion and garlic. Slice the onion into strips and finely chop the garlic.
Dice the courgette and aubergine into 2x2cm dice.
Pierce the tomatoes with a sharp knife.
Mix all the vegetables together with the chickpeas, olive oil, rosemary and balsamic vinegar and season with salt and pepper.
Roast everything in the oven on a baking sheet with baking paper for 20-25 mins or until tender and golden.
Mix in the picked basil and season with finely grated lemon zest and juice, salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/Gas Mark 6.
Drizzle the beetroot (skin on) with oil and season with salt. Wrap in aluminium foil.
Bake the beetroot for 45-50 mins until tender.
Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2x2cm cubes. Toss with olive oil, salt and pepper. Place on a baking tray lined with baking paper and bake for 25-30 mins until tender and golden.
Rinse and cook the quinoa according to instructions. Let it sit in the pot with a lid on for around 10 mins to rest and then let cool.
Pour boiling water over the parsley and squeeze the liquid out of the leaves once cool. Chop the leaves and puree them with a little cold water. Season the puree with salt to taste.
Mix the quinoa and parsley puree and arrange the mixture like small mountaintops in bowls.
Season the cottage cheese with salt and pepper to taste.
Chop the pistachios.
Remove the skin from the beetroots and cut into bite-size pieces.
Arrange the beetroot, baked sweet potato and cottage cheese around the quinoa mountaintops. Top with the chopped pistachios and some freshly ground black pepper.

Cut the peeled potatoes in half crosswise. Set them cut-side down on the cutting board and cut them into 1/8-inch-thick slices. Cut the onion in half through the root, remove the outer layer, and slice into 1/8-inch-thick half-moon slices.

Heat the olive oil in an 8- or 9-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering but not smoking. Add the potatoes and onions, reduce the heat to low and cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potatoes are tender when pricked with the tip of a knife. Use a slotted spoon to remove the potatoes and onions from the oil to a plate, reserving the oil.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs with a pinch of salt. Add the potatoes to the egg mixture and mix gently.

Heat 2 tablespoons of the reserved olive oil in the pan over medium heat until shimmering. Add the egg and potato mixture and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the eggs set at the bottom, shaking the pan occasionally to prevent sticking.

Set a plate larger than the pan over the top and quickly but carefully flip the pan to invert the omelette onto the plate. Add another tablespoon of oil to the skillet, then gently slide the omelette back into the pan, uncooked side down, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until just set.
Turn the omelette out onto a plate. Serve warm or at room temperature, cut into wedges, with the crusty bread.
Toss the sweet potato in oil, cumin and a little salt, then roast at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly charred.
Warm the black beans in a small pan with a pinch of cumin, mashing about half of them for texture.
Warm the corn tortillas in a dry pan for 20-30 seconds per side until pliable.
Fill each tortilla with black beans, roasted sweet potato and a handful of cabbage slaw.
Top with sliced avocado, a squeeze of lime and chopped coriander.
Mash the black beans lightly and spread over one flour tortilla.
Scatter the grated cheddar on top and cover with the second tortilla.
Heat a dry frying pan over medium heat and cook the quesadilla for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with the salsa and sour cream.
Heat a large pot over medium heat and sauté the diced onion and garlic for 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add the turkey mince and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, for 5-6 minutes until browned.
Stir in the chili spices and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the diced tomatoes and kidney beans, bring to a simmer, and cook uncovered for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Cook the rice according to the packet instructions.
Serve the chili spooned over the rice.
Slice or shred the leftover roast chicken.
Reheat the roast potatoes and green beans (or carrots) in a hot oven or microwave until piping hot throughout.
Warm the gravy in a small pan or microwave, stirring occasionally.
Plate the chicken and vegetables, then pour the gravy over the top before serving.
Lay the tortilla flat and spread the hummus over the surface.
Layer the sliced turkey breast, spinach, tomato and cucumber down the centre.
Fold in the sides and roll the tortilla tightly into a wrap.
Slice in half and serve with the apple.
